title: Sprint Lab: Collaborative POC Facilitation Journal and Templates
authors_provenance: Created by Ava Patel; contributors: Miguel Santos (latency bench), Priya Shah (KMS notes), Noah Kim (failure simulations). Drafted as an internal facilitator playbook and experiment journal for recurring POC sprint runs.
body:
Purpose - Quick lightweight playbook for running a 1-day customer POC sprint that mixes hands-on lab experiments + decision checkpoints. Focus is on validating deployment assumptions (latency/cost/fallback) and delivering a clear handoff for Dedicated/Private follow-up.

High-level agenda (8 hours)
1) 0:00-0:20 — Kickoff and success criteria
   - Introductions (customer + SE team)
   - Prime question: what decision do we want to make by EOD? (deploy path / SLA target / cost target)
   - Capture 2-3 measurable success criteria (latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, correct fallback behavior)

2) 0:20-0:50 — Architecture walkthrough & constraints
   - Quick diagram on whiteboard (hosted vs dedicated vs private options)
   - Data security constraints (PII, network restrictions, KMS)
   - Outstanding questions (list) — note as follow-ups

3) 0:50-1:30 — Mini-lab 1: Latency microbenchmark (engineer-led)
   - Setup: fixed prompt set + sequence-length samples (short/medium/long)
   - Run 3 model variants (base, quantized, small-context optimized)
   - Measure: cold-start, steady-state p50/p95, 99th-percentile tails
   - Artifact: csv of token rates + latency percentiles; screenshot of flame/trace if available

4) 1:30-2:15 — Mini-lab 2: Cost and throughput exploration (platform-led)
   - Simulated traffic profiles (burst vs steady)
   - Compare batching strategies and cache hit assumptions
   - Produce rough cost estimates for 100k tokens/day at observed batch sizes

5) 2:15-2:30 — Break and quick synthesis

6) 2:30-3:30 — Mini-lab 3: Failure & fallback drill (SRE + customer app engineer)
   - Simulate model endpoint OOM, region down, and degraded throughput
   - Validate automatic fallback to cheaper/compatible model variant and region failover path
   - Confirm observability hooks (traces, logs, cost alerts) trigger appropriately

7) 3:30-4:15 — Product/Business alignment: quality vs cost tradeoffs
   - Walk hypothetical A/B: higher-cost model vs quantized model with prompt engineering
   - Capture customer preference and acceptable quality delta (qualitative + small eval set)

8) 4:15-5:00 — Decision checkpoint: recommended deployment pattern & risks
   - Use a 2-column decision board: Recommendation + Confidence + Key risks + Mitigations
   - Agree on next steps (follow-up tickets, Dedicated sizing, compliance kickoff)

9) 5:00-5:30 — Handoff and wrap
   - Assign owners for follow-ups and timeline
   - Deliverables: artifact bundle (benchmarks, cost estimates, config snippets, slide summary)

Slide skeleton (10 slides) with speaker prompts
- Slide 1: Title + Team and Outcome (speaker: facilitator) — state the EOD decision we will drive to
- Slide 2: Agenda and roles (speaker: facilitator) — who does what and timeboxes
- Slide 3: Baseline architecture / constraints (speaker: engineer) — network/KMS/data notes
- Slide 4: Latency lab summary (speaker: bench engineer) — three charts, one sentence takeaways
- Slide 5: Cost/throughput summary (speaker: platform) — cost per 1k tokens by config
- Slide 6: Failure drill outcomes (speaker: SRE) — what failed, what recovered, gaps
- Slide 7: Quality tradeoff sample (speaker: product/pm) — 3 example prompts plus outputs
- Slide 8: Recommendation & deployment pattern (speaker: lead SE) — config snippets (batching, quantization level)
- Slide 9: Risks & mitigations (speaker: security/compliance) — top 5 risks with owners
- Slide 10: Next steps & owners (speaker: facilitator) — timeline and deliverables link

Facilitator notes / cues
- Keep labs short and instrumented; prefer 3 representative prompts over long lists.
- If latency numbers look good early, pivot more time to failure/fallback lab — that's where production surprises happen.
- Capture any ad-hoc customer requests as tickets with priority tags; don't let the agenda balloon.
- Use the whiteboard to expose implicit assumptions (e.g., cache hit rate, average sequence length).

Materials checklist (pre-work, what to prep)
- Customer: sample prompt set (3-15 prompts), representative payload sizes, network access window
- SE team: pre-provisioned test keys, small harness for traffic shaping, cost estimator sheet
- SRE: runbook template for fallback, prebuilt tracing dashboard link

Hypotheses to test (write these as 1-liners)
- H1: With prefix caching enabled, p95 latency for customer prompt set will drop by >= 30%
- H2: Quantized model will reduce per-token cost by >= 40% with < 8% quality delta on eval set
- H3: Auto-failover to region-b will increase error surface but reduce outage time by 70%

Measurement plan (what we record)
- Latency: p50, p95, p99, tail latencies during cold start and steady state
- Cost: tokens consumed, GPU-hours estimate, predicted monthly cost at 100k/day
- Quality: small eval pass rate, qualitative customer acceptance notes

Customer-facing deliverables (post-session)
- One-page summary (slide deck) with key numbers and recommended next-step (1-2 pages)
- Artifact zip with raw csvs, minimal config snips for Dedicated/Private, and runbook notes
- Follow-up ticket list (Jira) and proposed timeline for a pilot or dedicated sizing review

Facilitator journal (notes to self)
- 2025-09-12 run notes: customer had unexpected proxy requirement; needed a 30m extra to get networking agreement - flag as prework item next time.
- Observed: caching assumptions were optimistic; real hit-rate was 22% not 60% (we need pre-session sample to estimate).
- Good: fallback demo convinced them more than numbers did - prioritize scripted failure demos.
- TODO: make a 15-min 'networking checklist' pre-call document to send 48h before workshop.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Security wants an example KMS integration diagram for Private that shows key rotation cadence - action: Priya to draft by 2025-10-06.
- Need a clear billing example for Dedicated with burst vs reserved buckets - action: finance to provide sample by next week.
- Investigate a smaller sample harness that can be given to customers to self-run 1-hour pre-checks.

Quick templates (copy/paste useful snippets)
- Decision board header: 'Recommendation | Confidence (low/med/high) | Key risk | Mitigation | Owner'
- Failure demo script: '1) induce OOM on model-A; 2) confirm model-B activation; 3) verify error surfacing in customer dashboard'
- Pre-call networking checklist bullets: 'VPN endpoint available? CIDR allowlist provided? TLS inspection in path? Any outbound proxy?'

Notes to keep this different from other playbooks
- This doc treats the POC as an experiment lab with explicit hypotheses and quick failure drills rather than a feature demo.
- Emphasis on short, instrumented micro-labs and a facilitator journal for improving repeated runs.

End of doc
